text:
Sam: Noticed weird cluster churn in us-east1b starting ~01:20 UTC. Small GPU jobs stuck Pending while reserved pool nodes sit idle. Anyone digging?
Riya: Yeah, saw >80 tiny-gpu Pending. Kube-scheduler trace shows repeated schedule failures with "no suitable leader for gang" and anti-affinity score flips.
Jordan: Observed repeated node taint oscillation on a set of nodes: `gpu-shelf=reserved:NoSchedule` being re-applied then removed by the autoscaler controller during node health checks. Logs: 
```
I0402 01:21:03 autoscaler: node/node-usb3 patched taints [gpu-shelf=reserved:NoSchedule]
I0402 01:21:04 healthcheck: node-usb3 nic-firmware-warning -> mark NotReady
I0402 01:21:05 autoscaler: node/node-usb3 removed taint [gpu-shelf=reserved:NoSchedule]
```
Sam: Autoscaler removing the reserved taint means scheduler considers those nodes for generic placement, but then healthcheck flips NotReady and kubelet reapplies something. The net effect is pods bounce and small pods can't pack due to strong podAntiAffinity rules for NVLINK locality.
Kai: Packet from node health: NIC firmware reporting micro-drop and kernel logs show `mlx5_hw_err` transient which triggers healthcheck. The autoscaler reacts by untainting to allow eviction/migration, but that interacts poorly with our gang-scheduling assumptions.
Riya: So fragmentation arises: pods land on different nodes (no NVLINK), later get evicted when node flaps, come back Pending, and scheduler avoids colocated placement because of anti-affinity scoring. Circular.
Jordan: Prom query for the spike: `sum(increase(kube_pod_pending[5m])) by (node)` and `count(node:kube_node_status_condition{condition=\"Ready\",status=\"false\"}) by (node)`
Kai: Quick mitigation: 1) Temporarily lower podAntiAffinity weight for tiny-gpu class to allow looser packing 2) Add toleration `firmware-flap=true:NoSchedule` to the reserved pool nodes so autoscaler doesn't untaint them during transient flaps.
Sam: Agreed. Can we push both canaries? I can flip anti-affinity weight in the scheduler-config map for a canary namespace. Riya, can you add toleration to two reserved nodes?
Riya: Patching 2 nodes now: `kubectl patch node node-us-eastb-07 -p '{"spec":{"taints":[{"key":"firmware-flap","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}'` and annotate canary.
Infra-bot: Firmware bump available: `mlx5-fw-v2.1.4`. Recommendation: schedule rolling update for affected rack after stabilizing pending queue.
Jordan: We should not apply firmware mid-incident unless we drain explicitly. Plan: stabilize scheduling -> drain -> firmware update -> rejoin.
SRE-bot: Incident INC-5901 created for us-east1b tiny-gpu Pending surge. Owner: @oncall-sre.
Sam: Can we throttle the batch queue for 20m to avoid creating more fragmentation? I'll pause the job submitter.
Riya: Patch done on 2 nodes, scheduler canary applied. Watching Pending count.
Jordan: Pending dropped from 86 -> 22 in 12m. Some evictions continue but at much lower rate.
Kai: Added a temporary evict-hook to prevent evictions for pods with label `workload=tiny-gpu` during the stabilizing window. Command: `kubectl label pod -l app=tiny-gpu evict-protect=true --all` (canary-only).
Sam: Nice. Long-term followups: 1) autoscaler should not remove reserved taints on transient health signals 2) add CI test that simulates node-taint-oscillation and ensures scheduler still packs NVLINK-bound gangs 3) firmware monitoring + proactive replacement for racks with repeated `mlx5_hw_err`.
Riya: Filing RFC for autoscaler behavior change and CI test. Putting links in the incident.
Jordan: We'll schedule a controlled firmware rollout next week for impacted racks after postmortem.
SRE-bot: INC-5901 status -> mitigated.
Sam: Thanks team. Let's track cost delta (idle reserved pool) and add to the postmortem.
Kai: I'll collect `kube_node_labels{label_gpu_shelf="reserved"}` and `sum(rate(kube_pod_evicts_total[5m]))` for the timeline.
Riya: Good catch everyone — please ping if anything regresses. :eyes:
